$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-09-02 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 5876aff6. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v28 index for sub2api (INDEX e1a85bba) built by publish-tee-images run 33596517563 from commit 8971b5157; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin (INDEX cef1d03d) because deploy/attestor was not touched, and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, osImageHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release - the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. Landing page only: no backend code, no migrations. Two changes. First, the site now carries two films instead of one, and each sits beside the thing it talks about - the consumer film inside the section on how the gateway is used, the provider film inside the section on sharing a subscription. Previously a single film occupied its own block at the very bottom, which a reader reached only after passing the consumer, pricing and provider sections; it had no context by the time they arrived. The anchor that block carried was removed with it, since no navigation entry pointed at it. The provider film ships in Chinese and English and follows the interface language, falling back to English for any future locale rather than composing a URL that does not exist. Its caption deliberately does not claim the film explains the rules: it is a promotional piece, and copy promising that it covers where credentials live and how earnings are computed would set up an expectation the film does not meet - costly with an audience that is being asked to hand over a subscription credential. The caption says what it is and points at the blocks below, which do carry the rules. Second, model copy moved from Claude Fable 5 to 5.1 in six strings plus the architecture diagram and a hero stat; changing only the banner would leave the same page contradicting itself. The claim is verified: after proof-v26 the production models endpoint returns claude-fable-5-1. Note that three invite-share templates elsewhere in the dashboard still say Fable 5, and one of them still quotes half the official API price, which is a stale figure from before the move to 14 percent; they were left untouched in this release and remain outstanding. A pre-existing defect in the video component surfaced while testing the language switch: the source-change handler cleared the resume position and then called reload, which re-read the position from the element that was still playing, so a new source began at the previous one's timestamp - past the end entirely when the two differ in length. Reload now takes a flag; stall-retry keeps the position, a source change does not. Earlier in this line: proof-v27 (footer contact rail, X account), v26 (upstream sync through v0.1.185 and beyond, Claude Fable 5.1), v24 (pricing copy at 14 percent and a 50 percent revenue share), v23, v22, v21, v20, v19, v18, v17, v16/v15. osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation, and the control plane confirms is_dev false after the rollout. A full postgres backup was taken and verified beforehand - downloaded from S3, gzip-tested, 110 COPY sections. Frontend suite: 274 files and 2010 cases, type check and lint clean. This rollout completed in 93 seconds with no incident.
